name: discourse_moves
description: The coherence and signposting machinery of connected prose: RST-style relations between spans, signposting and metadiscourse moves, transition families and thematic-progression links, framing choices, and moves that manage the reader — each with the cue words and phrases that typically realize it.

coherence_relations.name: elaboration
coherence_relations.definition: A satellite span adds detail about the nucleus — a part, an attribute, an instance, or a further specification of the same situation.
coherence_relations.effect: Deepens without changing subject; the default relation in expository prose.

coherence_relations.name: instantiation
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite gives one or more cases of the general situation described in the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: Grounds a generalization in something a reader can picture or check.

coherence_relations.name: specification
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite describes the same event or entity as the nucleus at a finer grain, without adding a new event.
coherence_relations.effect: Zooms in; the reader understands it as the same thing seen closer.

coherence_relations.name: restatement
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite re-expresses the nucleus in different words at roughly the same level of generality.
coherence_relations.effect: Second chance at a difficult sentence; also a rhythm device.

coherence_relations.name: equivalence
coherence_relations.definition: Two spans describe the same situation from different perspectives, neither subordinate to the other.
coherence_relations.effect: Holds two descriptions in parallel so the reader can see they refer to one thing.

coherence_relations.name: summary
coherence_relations.definition: Coherence-relation sense (RST): a short satellite restates a longer nucleus in compressed form. Distinct from the narratological summary, which is a ratio of story time to discourse time.
coherence_relations.effect: Gives the reader something portable after a dense stretch.

coherence_relations.name: interpretation
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite places the nucleus in a framework not otherwise implied by it, saying what it amounts to.
coherence_relations.effect: Converts a fact into a meaning; the writer's reading becomes visible as a reading.

coherence_relations.name: evaluation
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite assesses the nucleus — good or bad, adequate or not, important or trivial.
coherence_relations.effect: Supplies the writer's judgment explicitly rather than smuggling it into description.

coherence_relations.name: background
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite supplies information the reader needs in order to make sense of the nucleus, without which the nucleus is opaque.
coherence_relations.effect: Prevents comprehension failure at the cost of momentum.

coherence_relations.name: circumstance
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite sets the temporal, spatial, or situational frame within which the nucleus is to be interpreted.
coherence_relations.effect: Anchors an event; often carried by a fronted adverbial.

coherence_relations.name: preparation
coherence_relations.definition: A satellite that precedes the nucleus and readies the reader for it without stating its content.
coherence_relations.effect: Creates a small expectation the nucleus then fills.

coherence_relations.name: motivation
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite increases the reader's desire to perform the action described in the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: The persuasive half of instruction: not why it works but why bother.

coherence_relations.name: enablement
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite increases the reader's ability to perform the action in the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: Supplies the means rather than the reason; standard in procedural writing.

coherence_relations.name: solutionhood
coherence_relations.definition: The nucleus presents a solution to a problem, need, or question stated in the satellite.
coherence_relations.effect: The organizing relation of problem-solution prose.

coherence_relations.name: evidence
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite increases the reader's belief in the nucleus by supplying observation or data.
coherence_relations.effect: Distinct from justify: it supports the claim, not the writer's right to make it.

coherence_relations.name: justify
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite increases the reader's acceptance of the writer's right to present the nucleus at all.
coherence_relations.effect: Defends the act of asserting rather than the assertion itself.

coherence_relations.name: concession
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite grants something apparently incompatible with the nucleus, which the nucleus nonetheless survives.
coherence_relations.effect: Signals fair dealing and pre-empts the reader's counterexample.

coherence_relations.name: antithesis
coherence_relations.definition: Coherence-relation sense (RST): the satellite states a position the writer rejects, so that the nucleus is preferred by contrast. Distinct from the figure, which is a matter of parallel grammatical form.
coherence_relations.effect: Sharper than concession: the satellite is not granted, it is set up to be refused.

coherence_relations.name: contrast
coherence_relations.definition: Two spans of equal status differ on one or more dimensions while being alike in others.
coherence_relations.effect: Multi-nuclear; neither side subordinates the other.

coherence_relations.name: similarity
coherence_relations.definition: Two spans of equal status are presented as alike in a specified respect.
coherence_relations.effect: Invites the reader to carry a judgment from one case to the other.

coherence_relations.name: comparison
coherence_relations.definition: Two spans are set against a common measure so that the reader can rank them.
coherence_relations.effect: Produces a scale rather than a mere difference.

coherence_relations.name: volitional cause
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite gives the reason an agent chose to bring about the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: Attributes intention; the reader reads the event as a decision.

coherence_relations.name: volitional result
coherence_relations.definition: The nucleus is an action an agent took, and the satellite is the outcome that action was meant to produce.
coherence_relations.effect: Closes the loop on intention.

coherence_relations.name: non-volitional cause
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite gives a cause of the nucleus in which no agent's intention is involved.
coherence_relations.effect: Renders the event as mechanism rather than choice — a consequential framing decision.

coherence_relations.name: non-volitional result
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite is an unintended consequence of the situation in the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: The shape of side effects, blowback, and unanticipated harm.

coherence_relations.name: purpose
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite states the end for which the action in the nucleus is undertaken.
coherence_relations.effect: Answers 'what for', which readers ask before 'how'.

coherence_relations.name: means
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite names the method by which the nucleus is accomplished.
coherence_relations.effect: Answers 'how', and often carries the technical content.

coherence_relations.name: manner
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite characterizes the way in which the situation in the nucleus occurs.
coherence_relations.effect: Adds quality without adding an event.

coherence_relations.name: condition
coherence_relations.definition: The nucleus obtains only if the situation in the satellite obtains.
coherence_relations.effect: Fences a claim; the honest way to make a large statement.

coherence_relations.name: otherwise
coherence_relations.definition: The nucleus obtains only if the satellite does not; states the alternative branch.
coherence_relations.effect: Supplies the fork the reader was about to ask about.

coherence_relations.name: unless
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite names the single circumstance that would defeat the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: Marks a defeasible claim and names its defeater.

coherence_relations.name: unconditional
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite names a circumstance that would ordinarily be expected to affect the nucleus, and denies that it does.
coherence_relations.effect: Strengthens a claim by pre-emptively surviving the obvious objection.

coherence_relations.name: disjunction
coherence_relations.definition: Two or more spans present alternatives of equal status.
coherence_relations.effect: Lays out the option space before narrowing it.

coherence_relations.name: substitution
coherence_relations.definition: One span is presented in place of another that is denied or set aside.
coherence_relations.effect: Corrects course inside a sentence: not this, that.

coherence_relations.name: exception
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite removes a case from the scope of the nucleus.
coherence_relations.effect: Preserves a generalization by carving out what would break it.

coherence_relations.name: conjunction
coherence_relations.definition: Spans of equal status combine to describe a situation neither describes alone.
coherence_relations.effect: Flat addition; the least directive of the relations.

coherence_relations.name: list
coherence_relations.definition: Parallel spans of equal status presented as members of a set, often numbered.
coherence_relations.effect: Signals completeness and lets the reader track progress through it.

coherence_relations.name: sequence
coherence_relations.definition: Spans describe events in temporal succession, one after the other.
coherence_relations.effect: The backbone of narrative and procedure.

coherence_relations.name: synchrony
coherence_relations.definition: Spans describe events overlapping in time.
coherence_relations.effect: Creates simultaneity, and with it, dramatic irony.

coherence_relations.name: result
coherence_relations.definition: The satellite states what the nucleus brought about, with the causal direction running forward from nucleus to satellite.
coherence_relations.effect: Reads as consequence rather than explanation.

coherence_relations.name: attribution
coherence_relations.definition: One span reports the source of the content of another — who said, thought, or found it.
coherence_relations.effect: Separates the claim from the writer's own commitment to it.

coherence_relations.name: topic shift
coherence_relations.definition: An abrupt move to a new subject with the seam marked so it does not read as incoherence.
coherence_relations.effect: Legitimate change of subject; unmarked, it reads as a lost thread.

coherence_relations.name: question-answer pair
coherence_relations.definition: One span poses a question that the following span answers, both belonging to the writer.
coherence_relations.effect: Dramatizes inquiry and controls the order in which the reader wants things.

signposting_moves.name: forecast the structure
signposting_moves.definition: Tell the reader in advance how the piece or section is organized and in what order it will proceed.
signposting_moves.effect: Makes long-form navigable; sets an expectation that must then be honored.
cues: this chapter proceeds in three parts

signposting_moves.name: state the aim
signposting_moves.definition: Say explicitly what the piece is trying to establish or do.
signposting_moves.effect: Lets a reader decide early whether to keep reading, and on what terms to judge it.

signposting_moves.name: announce the topic
signposting_moves.definition: Name the subject of the upcoming stretch without yet advancing a claim about it.
signposting_moves.effect: Orientation only; cheap and clear.

signposting_moves.name: preview the section
signposting_moves.definition: Summarize what the coming section will establish before establishing it.
signposting_moves.effect: Trades suspense for comprehension; correct in reference and technical writing.
cues: the argument of this section is

signposting_moves.name: number the parts
signposting_moves.definition: Attach explicit ordinals to the components of an argument or list.
signposting_moves.effect: Gives the reader a count to hold and a sense of progress.

signposting_moves.name: label the current step
signposting_moves.definition: Name where in the announced structure the reader currently is.
signposting_moves.effect: Reorients a reader who joined late or put the book down.
cues: this is the second of the three

signposting_moves.name: mark the halfway point
signposting_moves.definition: Note that the argument has reached a structural midpoint or pivot in its plan.
signposting_moves.effect: Renews attention by showing the shape of what remains.

signposting_moves.name: recall an earlier point
signposting_moves.definition: Bring a previously established point back into view before building on it.
signposting_moves.effect: Removes the need for the reader to hold everything in memory.

signposting_moves.name: summarize so far
signposting_moves.definition: Compress everything established up to this point into a short restatement.
signposting_moves.effect: Consolidation before a turn; standard at section joints.

signposting_moves.name: mark a digression
signposting_moves.definition: Flag that the next stretch departs from the main line.
signposting_moves.effect: Buys permission for necessary background without the reader losing the thread.
cues: before going on, a word about

signposting_moves.name: close a digression
signposting_moves.definition: Explicitly end a departure and re-enter the main argument.
signposting_moves.effect: Without it, the reader cannot tell that the detour has finished.
cues: with that out of the way

signposting_moves.name: mark the turn
signposting_moves.definition: Announce that the argument now changes direction.
signposting_moves.effect: Prevents a reversal from reading as inconsistency.
cues: so much for the case in favor

signposting_moves.name: signal the main claim
signposting_moves.definition: Mark a sentence as the load-bearing assertion of the piece or section.
signposting_moves.effect: Ensures the skimming reader does not miss the thesis.
cues: if you take one thing from this

signposting_moves.name: signal a subordinate point
signposting_moves.definition: Mark material as secondary so the reader weights it correctly.
signposting_moves.effect: Protects the hierarchy of an argument from being flattened.

signposting_moves.name: signal the counterargument
signposting_moves.definition: Announce that the opposing case is about to be stated in its own voice.
signposting_moves.effect: Stops the reader from mistaking the opponent's view for the writer's.
cues: the case against runs as follows

signposting_moves.name: signal that an objection is coming
signposting_moves.definition: Warn that the writer knows the obvious complaint and will reach it shortly.
signposting_moves.effect: Buys patience from a reader who would otherwise object now.
cues: I return to this objection below

signposting_moves.name: signal the conclusion
signposting_moves.definition: Mark that the inferential work is finished and the result follows.
signposting_moves.effect: Tells the reader when to stop gathering and start judging.

signposting_moves.name: signal an example
signposting_moves.definition: Mark that what follows is an illustration rather than new evidence.
signposting_moves.effect: Prevents an example from being mistaken for proof.

signposting_moves.name: signal a change of scale
signposting_moves.definition: Announce a move between levels of abstraction or magnitude.
signposting_moves.effect: Prevents the whiplash of an unmarked zoom.
cues: at the level of the individual

signposting_moves.name: signal a change of time frame
signposting_moves.definition: Mark a jump backward or forward in the period under discussion.
signposting_moves.effect: Keeps chronology legible in a non-chronological treatment.

signposting_moves.name: cross-reference forward
signposting_moves.definition: Point the reader to material treated later.
signposting_moves.effect: Defers without dropping; the promise must be kept.

signposting_moves.name: cross-reference backward
signposting_moves.definition: Point the reader to material already treated.
signposting_moves.effect: Reuses established ground instead of restating it.

signposting_moves.name: point to a figure or table
signposting_moves.definition: Direct the reader to a display and say what to look at in it.
signposting_moves.effect: A figure without a reading instruction is usually skipped.
cues: note the gap in the second column

signposting_moves.name: point to an appendix
signposting_moves.definition: Move technical material out of the main line and tell the reader where it went.
signposting_moves.effect: Keeps the argument readable while remaining auditable.
cues: the derivation is in appendix B

signposting_moves.name: name the section
signposting_moves.definition: Use an explicit title, heading, or in-text name for a stretch of argument.
signposting_moves.effect: Gives the reader a handle for later reference.

signposting_moves.name: restate the question
signposting_moves.definition: Repeat the governing question at a distance from where it was posed.
signposting_moves.effect: Re-anchors a long argument to what it is for.

signposting_moves.name: flag the takeaway
signposting_moves.definition: Mark a sentence as the thing to remember from a section.
signposting_moves.effect: Serves the skimmer and the note-taker.

signposting_moves.name: flag the payoff
signposting_moves.definition: Announce that a setup laid earlier is about to be redeemed.
signposting_moves.effect: Rewards the reader for having carried material forward.
cues: this is why the definition mattered
here is where it pays off

signposting_moves.name: mark the scope boundary
signposting_moves.definition: State the limits of what the current discussion covers.
signposting_moves.effect: Blocks objections that are actually outside the terms of the piece.

signposting_moves.name: announce the method
signposting_moves.definition: State how the evidence was gathered or the analysis performed before presenting results.
signposting_moves.effect: Allows the reader to discount appropriately before being persuaded.

signposting_moves.name: announce the order of treatment
signposting_moves.definition: State the principle by which items will be sequenced — chronological, by importance, by category.
signposting_moves.effect: Removes the reader's suspicion that the order is arbitrary.

signposting_moves.name: signal parallel structure
signposting_moves.definition: Announce that several items will be treated the same way on the same dimensions.
signposting_moves.effect: Lets the reader predict the shape and compare across cases.
cues: for each of these I ask

signposting_moves.name: open a list
signposting_moves.definition: Announce that an enumeration is beginning and, ideally, how long it is.
signposting_moves.effect: The count is a promise of an ending; readers relax when they have one.

signposting_moves.name: close a list
signposting_moves.definition: Mark the last item as the last.
signposting_moves.effect: Prevents the reader from waiting for a fourth item that never comes.
cues: and that is the whole of it

signposting_moves.name: signal contrast with the previous point
signposting_moves.definition: Mark the incoming material as standing against what just preceded it.
signposting_moves.effect: The commonest transition in argument; effective in moderation.

signposting_moves.name: announce an aside
signposting_moves.definition: Introduce a remark the writer wants on record but outside the argument's load path.
signposting_moves.effect: Permits personality and stray observation without structural cost.
cues: it is worth noting in passing

signposting_moves.name: return to the main thread
signposting_moves.definition: Resume a line of argument suspended some distance back, naming it.
signposting_moves.effect: Redeems a suspended thread that would otherwise read as abandoned.
cues: to pick up the earlier thread

metadiscourse_moves.name: hedge a claim
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Reduce the writer's commitment to a proposition through modality or approximation.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Makes the claim survivable; the field's default posture for anything not settled.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: Stacked hedges read as evasion and are a recognized AI tell.

metadiscourse_moves.name: boost a claim
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Raise the writer's commitment above the neutral assertion, closing off dialogic alternatives.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Signals confidence and reduces the reader's sense that the matter is open.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: Boosting an underevidenced claim is the fastest way to lose an expert reader.

metadiscourse_moves.name: attribute to a source
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Locate the origin of the content in someone other than the writer.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Distributes responsibility for the claim and makes it checkable.

metadiscourse_moves.name: gloss a term
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Restate a technical or unfamiliar expression immediately in accessible words.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Lets the writer keep the precision of jargon without losing the lay reader.

metadiscourse_moves.name: restate in plain words
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Follow a dense or formal formulation with a deliberately plain paraphrase.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: A second entry point into a hard sentence.
cues: to say the same thing simply

metadiscourse_moves.name: gloss with an example
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Clarify a term or claim by supplying a case rather than a definition.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Ostensive definition; often faster than the analytic kind.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark surprise
metadiscourse_moves.definition: An attitude marker signaling that a finding is contrary to expectation.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Tells the reader which findings are news.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark importance
metadiscourse_moves.definition: An attitude marker singling out material as significant.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Directs the reader's weighting.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark agreement
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Signal alignment with a cited position or a reader's likely view.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Builds solidarity cheaply; also sets up a coming disagreement.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark regret or dismay
metadiscourse_moves.definition: An attitude marker registering the writer's discomfort with what is being reported.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Colors a fact without arguing about it.

metadiscourse_moves.name: self-mention as investigator
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Foreground the writer as the person who gathered the material.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Grounds evidence in a person who can be asked about it.

metadiscourse_moves.name: self-mention as guide
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Use first person for the discourse acts of the text itself rather than for its content.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Names the writer's structural choices as choices.

metadiscourse_moves.name: inclusive we
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Use a first-person plural that folds the reader into the writer's reasoning.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Makes the argument feel jointly performed rather than delivered.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: Slides easily into a false consensus the reader has not agreed to.

metadiscourse_moves.name: direct address to the reader
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Speak to the reader as 'you'.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Breaks the fourth wall of exposition; raises immediacy and obligation.

metadiscourse_moves.name: ask the reader a question
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Pose a question meant to be entertained by the reader rather than answered by the text.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Recruits the reader into the inquiry.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: A string of unanswered rhetorical questions reads as padding.

metadiscourse_moves.name: issue a directive
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Instruct the reader to perform a cognitive or physical act.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: The strongest engagement marker; forces participation.

metadiscourse_moves.name: appeal to shared knowledge
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Present a proposition as already known to the reader and the field.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Saves argument, and quietly constructs the community it appeals to.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: The reader who does not in fact know it is now excluded.

metadiscourse_moves.name: acknowledge a limitation
metadiscourse_moves.definition: State what the evidence, method, or argument cannot deliver.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Pre-empts the sharpest reader's first objection and makes the rest more credible.

metadiscourse_moves.name: attribute uncertainty to the field
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Locate doubt in the state of knowledge rather than in the writer's confidence.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Distinguishes 'nobody knows' from 'I am not sure', which readers otherwise conflate.

metadiscourse_moves.name: concede a point
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Grant an opposing claim outright before continuing.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Purchases credibility for the disagreement that follows.

metadiscourse_moves.name: signal personal stance
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Mark an assessment as the writer's own rather than as established fact.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Keeps opinion visible as opinion.

metadiscourse_moves.name: withhold stance
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Report without evaluation, often through impersonal or agentless construction.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Neutral register; also a way of hiding a judgment inside description.

metadiscourse_moves.name: background the agent
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Use passive or nominalized construction to remove the actor from the sentence.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Focuses on process — and, used badly, conceals responsibility.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: The characteristic move of institutional evasion; use knowingly.

metadiscourse_moves.name: foreground the agent
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Restore a named actor to the subject position of a sentence.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Restores accountability and usually shortens the sentence.

metadiscourse_moves.name: establish the territory
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Open by asserting the centrality, size, or activity of the research or subject area.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Tells the reader the subject is worth their time before making any claim about it.
cues: much attention has been paid to

metadiscourse_moves.name: indicate a gap
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Identify what prior work has not done, or has done wrongly.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Creates the space the piece will occupy; without it the piece has no reason to exist.

metadiscourse_moves.name: occupy the gap
metadiscourse_moves.definition: State what this piece does to fill the gap just identified.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Converts a criticism of the field into the writer's mandate.

metadiscourse_moves.name: preview findings
metadiscourse_moves.definition: State the principal results up front rather than making the reader wait for them.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Standard in scientific and executive writing; hostile to suspense, friendly to use.

metadiscourse_moves.name: announce novelty
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Claim that the material is new, unreported, or first.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Raises the stakes of the reading and invites checking.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: Easy to overclaim; a single prior instance sinks it.

metadiscourse_moves.name: claim significance
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Argue that a result matters beyond its immediate case.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Answers the 'so what', which readers ask before believing.

metadiscourse_moves.name: state a boundary condition
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Specify the circumstances under which a claim holds.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Converts a vulnerable universal into a defensible restricted claim.

metadiscourse_moves.name: quantify a generalization
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Replace an unquantified claim with an explicit proportion, count, or frequency.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Removes the slipperiness of 'many' and 'often'; the reader can now disagree precisely.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark evidential strength
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Say how good the supporting evidence is, separately from what it shows.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Lets the reader weight claims differently within a single argument.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark a hypothetical
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Flag material as supposed rather than asserted.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Permits reasoning about cases without asserting they occurred.

metadiscourse_moves.name: mark a definition as stipulative
metadiscourse_moves.definition: State that a term is being fixed for present purposes rather than reported from usage.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Blocks the objection that the word means something else elsewhere.

metadiscourse_moves.name: flag a technical sense
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Warn that an ordinary-looking word is being used in a specialist sense.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Prevents the reader's everyday meaning from silently corrupting the argument.

metadiscourse_moves.name: signal ironic distance
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Mark a word or phrase as belonging to someone else's vocabulary, not the writer's.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Criticizes a term without pausing to argue about it.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: Scare quotes at density read as sneering.

metadiscourse_moves.name: signal reported speech
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Mark words as another party's utterance, direct or indirect.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Keeps the boundary between voices legible.

metadiscourse_moves.name: distance from a source
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Report a claim while withholding endorsement of it.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Permits repeating contested material without owning it.

metadiscourse_moves.name: endorse a source
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Report a claim and explicitly signal agreement with or confidence in it.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: The writer's credibility becomes collateral for the source's.

metadiscourse_moves.name: endophoric reference
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Point to another part of the same text — a section, figure, note, or earlier phrase.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Turns a linear text into something navigable.

metadiscourse_moves.name: attribute to common opinion
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Ascribe a view to an unnamed general public or professional consensus.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Sets up a target that can be argued against without naming an opponent.
metadiscourse_moves.caution: Unsourced consensus claims are a favorite of lazy argument and are easily challenged.

metadiscourse_moves.name: date a claim
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Attach an explicit time index to an assertion whose truth is time-dependent.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Keeps a book honest as the world moves on.

metadiscourse_moves.name: localize a claim
metadiscourse_moves.definition: Attach an explicit jurisdiction, region, or population to a claim that would otherwise read as universal.
metadiscourse_moves.effect: Prevents a parochial finding from being read as a law of nature.

transition_families.name: additive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that add material of the same kind and status to what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Flat accumulation; the reader expects more of the same.

transition_families.name: adversative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that set the incoming material against what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Signals that the direction of the argument is about to change.

transition_families.name: concessive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that grant a point while signaling that it will not decide the matter.
transition_families.effect: Sets up a pivot; the reader waits for the 'but'.

transition_families.name: causal transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that present what follows as the reason for what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Points backward along the causal chain.

transition_families.name: consequential transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that present what follows as the result of what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Points forward along the causal chain.

transition_families.name: conditional transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that make what follows depend on a stated circumstance.
transition_families.effect: Fences the claim inside a hypothesis.

transition_families.name: exceptive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that remove a case from a stated generalization.
transition_families.effect: Protects a rule by naming its carve-out.

transition_families.name: illustrative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark what follows as an instance of what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Tells the reader to read the next span as a case, not new evidence.

transition_families.name: comparative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that place the incoming material alongside the preceding on a shared measure.
transition_families.effect: Invites the reader to rank rather than merely to note.

transition_families.name: temporal transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that locate what follows in time relative to what preceded.
transition_families.effect: The narrative spine; also the commonest way to fake causation.

transition_families.name: enumerative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark position within a counted series.
transition_families.effect: Gives the reader a place in a sequence and a promise of its end.

transition_families.name: spatial transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that organize material by position in space.
transition_families.effect: The backbone of description and of any argument organized by geography.

transition_families.name: summative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark a compressed restatement of what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Signals that no new material is coming, only consolidation.

transition_families.name: conclusive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark the end of the argument and the arrival of its verdict.
transition_families.effect: Distinct from summative: the reader is told to judge, not to review.

transition_families.name: resumptive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that pick up a thread suspended earlier.
transition_families.effect: Repairs the reader's sense of a promise outstanding.
cues: picking up where we left off

transition_families.name: clarifying transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark a restatement intended to remove ambiguity.
transition_families.effect: Signals that the previous formulation was insufficient, not that new content follows.

transition_families.name: reformulative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that recast the preceding material in a different frame or vocabulary.
transition_families.effect: Offers a second angle rather than a plainer version of the same one.

transition_families.name: corrective transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that withdraw or amend what was just said.
transition_families.effect: Enacts the writer thinking; used well, a mark of honesty.

transition_families.name: intensifying transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that add a stronger instance of the same point.
transition_families.effect: Escalates rather than merely adds.

transition_families.name: diminishing transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that reduce the weight of the incoming material relative to what preceded.
transition_families.effect: Keeps a minor point from reading as a major one.

transition_families.name: limiting transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that restrict the scope of a claim just made.
transition_families.effect: Retreats to defensible ground without abandoning the point.

transition_families.name: emphatic transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark the incoming material as the one to attend to.
transition_families.effect: Directs attention; loses force with repetition.

transition_families.name: alternative transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that offer another option of equal standing.
transition_families.effect: Opens the option space rather than narrowing it.

transition_families.name: purposive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark what follows as the end toward which the preceding was a means.
transition_families.effect: Answers 'what for'.

transition_families.name: evidential transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark the incoming material as support for the preceding claim.
transition_families.effect: Tells the reader to read the next span as proof rather than elaboration.

transition_families.name: digressive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that mark a step away from the main line.
transition_families.effect: Licenses a detour; must be paired with a resumptive.

transition_families.name: topic-shifting transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that move to a new subject without claiming a relation to the old one.
transition_families.effect: Honest about discontinuity, which is better than faking a link.

transition_families.name: appositive transitions
transition_families.definition: Connectives that introduce a renaming or expansion of the immediately preceding element.
transition_families.effect: Compresses a definition into the flow of a sentence.

transition_families.name: asyndetic juxtaposition
transition_families.definition: Placement of spans side by side with no connective, leaving the relation for the reader to infer.
transition_families.effect: Fastest and most trusting transition; also the one that risks incoherence.
transition_families.caution: Only works when the relation is genuinely obvious from content.

transition_families.name: lexical repetition link
transition_families.definition: Cohesion achieved by repeating a key noun or phrase from the previous sentence.
transition_families.effect: The plainest cohesive tie in English prose and the least noticed.

transition_families.name: pronominal link
transition_families.definition: Cohesion achieved by a pronoun pointing back to an antecedent in the previous span.
transition_families.effect: Economical; fails badly when more than one antecedent is available.

transition_families.name: demonstrative summary link
transition_families.definition: A demonstrative plus a summarizing noun that packages the previous span into a subject.
transition_families.effect: Lets a whole paragraph become the grammatical subject of the next sentence.

transition_families.name: given-new link
transition_families.definition: Beginning a sentence with information already in play and ending it with what is new.
transition_families.effect: The information-flow principle behind most sentences that feel easy to read.

transition_families.name: constant-theme progression
transition_families.definition: Successive sentences keep the same theme and vary what is said about it.
transition_families.effect: Holds a subject steady; the natural shape of a portrait or a definition.

transition_families.name: linear theme progression
transition_families.definition: The rheme of one sentence becomes the theme of the next, chaining forward.
transition_families.effect: Feels like reasoning in motion; each sentence hands the reader to the next.

transition_families.name: derived-theme progression
transition_families.definition: Successive themes are different sub-parts of a single overarching topic named earlier.
transition_families.effect: The shape of survey and classification passages.

transition_families.name: split-rheme progression
transition_families.definition: A sentence introduces two or more elements, and following sentences take each in turn.
transition_families.effect: Announces a branch and then walks it; strong for two-part comparisons.
cues: two problems arose. The first… The second…

framing_moves.name: frame as a problem
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject as a difficulty requiring resolution.
framing_moves.effect: Creates demand for the writer's remaining pages.

framing_moves.name: frame as a puzzle
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject as an anomaly that current understanding cannot explain.
framing_moves.effect: Recruits curiosity rather than alarm; better for readers resistant to advocacy.

framing_moves.name: frame as a story
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject through a sequence of events involving particular people.
framing_moves.effect: Converts an issue into something with characters and consequences.
cues: by the end of that year

framing_moves.name: frame as a choice
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject as a decision facing an identified party.
framing_moves.effect: Makes the reader an evaluator of options rather than a recipient of information.
cues: the question before us is whether

framing_moves.name: frame as a trade-off
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject as an exchange in which gains on one dimension cost something on another.
framing_moves.effect: Blocks the fantasy of a costless answer.

framing_moves.name: frame as a threshold question
framing_moves.definition: Argue that one prior question must be settled before anything else can be discussed.
framing_moves.effect: Controls the order of debate, which often decides it.

framing_moves.name: frame against the conventional view
framing_moves.definition: Define the position by what it contradicts in received opinion.
framing_moves.effect: Borrows the energy of the familiar view to launch the unfamiliar one.
framing_moves.caution: Requires that the conventional view actually be conventional.
cues: the standard story has it that

framing_moves.name: zoom out
framing_moves.definition: Enlarge the frame so the case at hand becomes an instance of a wider pattern.
framing_moves.effect: Raises stakes and generality in one move.

framing_moves.name: zoom in
framing_moves.definition: Narrow the frame from a general phenomenon to a single case examined closely.
framing_moves.effect: Makes an abstraction cost something to a nameable person.

framing_moves.name: reframe the question
framing_moves.definition: Accept that a question is being asked but argue it is the wrong one, and substitute another.
framing_moves.effect: Wins by changing the ground rather than by answering.
cues: asked that way, it has no answer

framing_moves.name: reject the frame
framing_moves.definition: Refuse the terms in which an issue has been posed, without offering a substitute question yet.
framing_moves.effect: Clears imported assumptions before building.
cues: the framing itself is the problem

framing_moves.name: name the phenomenon
framing_moves.definition: Give an unnamed but recurring pattern an explicit name.
framing_moves.effect: Naming makes a pattern discussable and countable; it is the writer's most durable contribution.
cues: there is no word for this, so

framing_moves.name: adopt the opponent's frame
framing_moves.definition: Argue the case entirely within the terms the other side prefers.
framing_moves.effect: A win on hostile ground is harder to dismiss than a win on your own.

framing_moves.name: metaphorical framing
framing_moves.definition: Structure understanding of the subject through a systematic metaphor carried across the passage.
framing_moves.effect: Metaphors bring entailments with them; the frame does argument silently.
framing_moves.caution: Audit what the metaphor implies — it will be read even where it was not meant.

framing_moves.name: analogical framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject as relevantly like a case the reader already has settled views about.
framing_moves.effect: Imports a whole judgment rather than a single implication.

framing_moves.name: historical framing
framing_moves.definition: Situate the subject in a lineage of earlier episodes.
framing_moves.effect: Makes a current event legible as recurrence rather than novelty.

framing_moves.name: counterfactual framing
framing_moves.definition: Establish significance by describing what would have happened otherwise.
framing_moves.effect: Isolates the contribution of the factor under discussion.

framing_moves.name: quantitative framing
framing_moves.definition: Introduce the subject through its magnitude — counts, rates, comparisons of scale.
framing_moves.effect: Establishes proportion before anecdote distorts it.
framing_moves.caution: The chosen denominator does most of the persuading; state it.

framing_moves.name: gain framing
framing_moves.definition: Present a course of action in terms of what will be gained by taking it.
framing_moves.effect: Encourages risk-averse choice; the standard framing for adoption.

framing_moves.name: loss framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the same course of action in terms of what will be lost by not taking it.
framing_moves.effect: Empirically more motivating, and more likely to be resented once noticed.

framing_moves.name: stakes framing
framing_moves.definition: Foreground who bears the consequences and how large they are.
framing_moves.effect: Answers 'why now' and 'why me'.
cues: the people who pay for this

framing_moves.name: moral framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject in terms of duty, harm, fairness, or desert.
framing_moves.effect: Shifts the argument from efficiency to obligation, changing what counts as a good answer.

framing_moves.name: procedural framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject in terms of whether the right process was followed.
framing_moves.effect: Available even when the substantive question is contested; the lawyer's frame.

framing_moves.name: boundary framing
framing_moves.definition: Define the subject by stating clearly what it is not.
framing_moves.effect: Prevents the argument from being answered as if it were a different argument.
cues: this is not a claim about

framing_moves.name: typology framing
framing_moves.definition: Introduce the subject as a set of distinguishable kinds rather than a single thing.
framing_moves.effect: Converts a stalemate about the whole into tractable questions about parts.

framing_moves.name: institutional framing
framing_moves.definition: Present events as the products of organizations, incentives, and rules rather than individual choice.
framing_moves.effect: Redirects blame and remedy from persons to structures.

framing_moves.name: personal-witness framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject through the writer's own presence at or involvement in it.
framing_moves.effect: Trades the authority of detachment for the authority of having been there.

framing_moves.name: temporal framing
framing_moves.definition: Fix the subject by a before-and-after boundary that makes change the point.
framing_moves.effect: Establishes that something happened, which most arguments assume and few show.

framing_moves.name: systems framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject as a set of interacting parts with feedback, delays, and emergent behavior.
framing_moves.effect: Explains outcomes nobody chose; resists single-cause and single-culprit readings.

framing_moves.name: risk framing
framing_moves.definition: Present the subject in terms of probability and magnitude of adverse outcomes.
framing_moves.effect: Makes uncertainty explicit rather than resolving it by rhetoric.

reader_management_moves.name: anticipate an objection
reader_management_moves.definition: Raise the reader's likely counterargument before the reader does, and address it.
reader_management_moves.effect: Converts a private resistance into a handled one.

reader_management_moves.name: preempt a misreading
reader_management_moves.definition: Name a wrong interpretation the sentence invites and rule it out.
reader_management_moves.effect: Cheaper than correcting the misreading later, and it shows the writer has anticipated it.

reader_management_moves.name: define a term
reader_management_moves.definition: Supply the meaning of a term the argument will rest on, before resting on it.
reader_management_moves.effect: Prevents a dispute about substance from becoming a dispute about words.

reader_management_moves.name: calibrate confidence
reader_management_moves.definition: State the degree of confidence in a claim explicitly, ideally in comparative or numerical terms.
reader_management_moves.effect: More informative than hedging: the reader learns how much to update.
cues: the weakest claim in this chapter

reader_management_moves.name: state what is not covered
reader_management_moves.definition: Tell the reader which adjacent questions the piece deliberately leaves alone.
reader_management_moves.effect: Prevents the reader from waiting for a treatment that will never arrive.
cues: another book could be written on

reader_management_moves.name: promise a later payoff
reader_management_moves.definition: Ask the reader to accept or carry something now on the assurance it will pay off later.
reader_management_moves.effect: Buys patience for material that is dull in isolation.
reader_management_moves.caution: A promise not kept is the failure readers remember.
cues: this will matter in chapter six

reader_management_moves.name: deliver on a promise
reader_management_moves.definition: Explicitly redeem an earlier commitment, marking it as the thing that was promised.
reader_management_moves.effect: Rewards the reader's trust and makes the structure feel designed.
cues: this is why I asked you to remember

reader_management_moves.name: warn of difficulty
reader_management_moves.definition: Tell the reader that the next stretch is hard, and why it is worth it.
reader_management_moves.effect: Readers tolerate difficulty they were warned about far better than difficulty they were not.
cues: the next few pages are technical
this is the hardest idea in the book

reader_management_moves.name: offer an off-ramp
reader_management_moves.definition: Tell the reader they may skip a section without losing the argument.
reader_management_moves.effect: Keeps a general reader moving while serving the specialist.
cues: readers uninterested in the derivation can skip to
the rest of this section is optional

reader_management_moves.name: offer a shortcut summary
reader_management_moves.definition: Provide a compressed version of a long treatment for readers who will not read all of it.
reader_management_moves.effect: Serves the skimmer without diluting the full account.

reader_management_moves.name: check comprehension
reader_management_moves.definition: Pause to test whether the reader is still following, usually by restating the state of play as a question.
reader_management_moves.effect: Catches the reader who has lost the thread before they abandon the text.
cues: the point to have grasped is

reader_management_moves.name: restate for the skimmer
reader_management_moves.definition: Repeat the essential claim in a form that survives being read out of context.
reader_management_moves.effect: Long-form is read discontinuously; the claim must be recoverable at several points.

reader_management_moves.name: acknowledge resistance
reader_management_moves.definition: Name the reader's likely emotional or ideological reluctance rather than only their intellectual objection.
reader_management_moves.effect: Defuses the reaction that would otherwise block the argument regardless of its merits.
cues: if you have worked in this field, you may bristle

reader_management_moves.name: validate the reader's intuition
reader_management_moves.definition: Confirm that the reader's instinct was right before refining or complicating it.
reader_management_moves.effect: Costs nothing and buys attention for the complication.
cues: you are not wrong to think

reader_management_moves.name: correct a misconception
reader_management_moves.definition: State a widely held belief, show it is false, and supply the correct account.
reader_management_moves.effect: Clears interference; a reader holding the wrong model cannot absorb the right one.
reader_management_moves.caution: Repeating the false claim prominently can reinforce it; lead with the correction.

reader_management_moves.name: lower the temperature
reader_management_moves.definition: Deliberately de-escalate the emotional register of a contested subject.
reader_management_moves.effect: Makes it possible for a reader on the other side to keep reading.

reader_management_moves.name: raise urgency
reader_management_moves.definition: Attach a deadline, a rising cost, or a closing window to the argument.
reader_management_moves.effect: Moves a reader from agreement to action.
reader_management_moves.caution: Manufactured urgency, once detected, discredits everything around it.
cues: by the time the review reports

reader_management_moves.name: give permission to disagree
reader_management_moves.definition: Explicitly allow that the reader may reject the conclusion while accepting the analysis.
reader_management_moves.effect: Separates the reader's evaluation of the evidence from their loyalty to a position.
cues: the facts are the facts either way

reader_management_moves.name: invite the reader to test the claim
reader_management_moves.definition: Supply a check the reader can run themselves.
reader_management_moves.effect: Converts assertion into something falsifiable in the reader's own hands.

reader_management_moves.name: supply a mnemonic
reader_management_moves.definition: Give a compact device — an acronym, a rule of thumb, a rhyme — for retaining a structure.
reader_management_moves.effect: Improves retention of material the reader must carry across chapters.

reader_management_moves.name: supply a worked example
reader_management_moves.definition: Run the whole procedure or argument once on a concrete case, showing every step.
reader_management_moves.effect: For procedures, one worked case teaches more than three paragraphs of description.

reader_management_moves.name: supply a lay analogy
reader_management_moves.definition: Offer a non-specialist comparison for a technical mechanism, and mark where it breaks down.
reader_management_moves.effect: Lets the general reader hold the shape of the idea without the machinery.

reader_management_moves.name: flag jargon
reader_management_moves.definition: Mark a term as specialist vocabulary the reader is not expected to know.
reader_management_moves.effect: Reassures the reader that incomprehension is expected, not a failing.
cues: an unlovely word, but the standard one

reader_management_moves.name: translate jargon
reader_management_moves.definition: Replace or accompany a technical term with its ordinary-language equivalent throughout.
reader_management_moves.effect: Keeps a specialist argument readable outside the specialty.
cues: what lawyers call X — really just
the everyday word for this is

reader_management_moves.name: manage expectations about evidence
reader_management_moves.definition: Tell the reader in advance what kind and quality of evidence is available on the question.
reader_management_moves.effect: Stops the reader expecting a randomized trial where only case records exist.

reader_management_moves.name: disclose an interest
reader_management_moves.definition: State the writer's material or institutional stake in the subject.
reader_management_moves.effect: Costs less to volunteer than to have discovered.

reader_management_moves.name: credit prior work
reader_management_moves.definition: Attribute an idea or finding to whoever established it first.
reader_management_moves.effect: Ethical baseline; also situates the writer as a participant rather than an outsider.

reader_management_moves.name: name the audience
reader_management_moves.definition: State who the writing is for.
reader_management_moves.effect: Lets the right reader lean in and the wrong reader leave without resentment.

reader_management_moves.name: signal the difficulty has passed
reader_management_moves.definition: Tell the reader the hard stretch is over.
reader_management_moves.effect: Releases held attention; the reader who was struggling can re-engage.
cues: from here it is plain sailing

reader_management_moves.name: pace the reader
reader_management_moves.definition: Insert a deliberate slack passage after a dense one — an anecdote, a short section, a change of register.
reader_management_moves.effect: Sustained density loses readers regardless of quality.
cues: a short chapter for a reason

reader_management_moves.name: pre-commit to a standard of proof
reader_management_moves.definition: State in advance what evidence would settle the question, before showing what is available.
reader_management_moves.effect: Prevents the writer from moving the goalposts and shows the reader they will not be.
cues: I would accept the opposite if
what would change my mind is

reader_management_moves.name: concede the strongest counterevidence
reader_management_moves.definition: Present the single most damaging fact against the argument rather than leaving it to a critic.
reader_management_moves.effect: Enormous credibility gain; also removes the critic's best opening move.
cues: the hardest case for my argument is
the one finding I cannot explain

reader_management_moves.name: solicit trust through candor
reader_management_moves.definition: Volunteer a failure, error, or change of mind of the writer's own.
reader_management_moves.effect: Admitted error is the cheapest credibility available and the least imitable.
cues: my first draft argued the opposite

reader_management_moves.name: explain the omission
reader_management_moves.definition: Say why an obvious topic, case, or source has been left out.
reader_management_moves.effect: Distinguishes a decision from an oversight, which the reader cannot otherwise tell apart.
cues: the obvious case is missing because
it is not here for a reason
